transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-10-27 16:00 UTC | Duration: 38m | Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Maya Patel (CISO Sequoia Health), Daniel Ortiz (Head Infra), Samantha Lee (Security Engineer)

[00:00] Alex Chen: ok thanks everyone for joining, appreciate you squeezing this in. we're here to walk through the pen test results and the remediation path, and then broader items — vuln mgmt, SDLC, patching cadence, plus questions on SOC2/ISO and KMS. Priya will run through the findings.

[00:28] Priya Nair: thanks Alex. hi Maya, Daniel, Sam. quick note — we shared the raw pen test PDF earlier, this is the annotated version with severity and suggested mitigations. i know there are a lot of details but i'll go high level first then drill into the three higher-risk items we flagged. audio may be a little spotty, sorry if i mumble.

[01:02] Maya Patel: yep all good, we got the file. happy for you to call out the big ones — CISO will want timeline and evidence for fixed items.

[01:20] Priya Nair: ok, top critical: 1) exposed admin console endpoint with weak auth headers — basically a misconfigured ingress rule in one staging cluster that was reachable from a public IP; 2) an auth bypass in a legacy internal microservice that doesn't use the platform RBAC properly; 3) outdated TLS config on the metrics endpoint that allowed weak ciphers in certain older clients. medium and low items are mainly info disclosure and minor config issues.

[02:03] Daniel Ortiz: that ingress thing — is that on your hosted environment or part of the private deployment we were vetting? i thought our POC was on dedicated, private VPC.

[02:17] Alex Chen: good question. the pen test targeted both environments in scope: the dedicated-reserved pool we spun up for you and the staging cluster in our hosted bucket for smoke tests. the exposed endpoint was in the staging cluster — not customer production — but still, we take ownership.

[02:40] Samantha Lee: ok glad that was staging. do you have an exploit timeline? how long was it reachable?

[02:51] Priya Nair: tester notes say about 12 hours during a mis-deploy window; we patched the ingress rule within 4 hours of discovery by the test team, then applied automated hardening scripts to the ingress controller. we'll share the audit logs showing the change.

[03:20] Maya Patel: audit logs — that's critical. we need tamper-evident logs and an indelible trail for SOC2. can you confirm the retention and whether logs include admin API calls?

[03:35] Alex Chen: yes. Redwood Console has route-level logging and admin action logs. for hosted we retain logs 90 days by default, can extend; for Dedicated and Private we support configurable retention and push to customer SIEM via secure forwarders. admin API calls are captured — we'll send the schema of the log events.

[04:05] Daniel Ortiz: is that push through a collector or direct syslog? we prefer a collector in VPC with TLS + mutual auth.

[04:16] Priya Nair: collector model — we offer a Fluent-bit/Fluentd sidecar pattern or direct secure-forwarding agent that uses mutual TLS to your SIEM. in Private deployments you can fully control the collector in your VPC.

[04:40] Maya Patel: cool. next, the auth bypass in the microservice — is that our code or something in Redwood's runtime?

[04:52] Priya Nair: that was in a Redwood-side integration component that adapts legacy auth headers for older clients. the issue was missing RBAC enforcement on a specific endpoint. fix: we've patched the component to validate tokens against our authz service, added unit tests, and added an integration check in our CI.

[05:18] Samantha Lee: unit tests + CI hooks sound good. can you outline the secure SDLC improvements you mentioned — like code scanning, dependency checks, PR gating?

[05:31] Alex Chen: sure. we run SAST on merge, dependency scanning with Snyk and internal SBOMs, container image scanning on our registry, and we have mandatory PR reviewers + security checklist for any infra changes. Priya, do you want to add patch cadence?

[05:50] Priya Nair: yeah. for infra/OS images we have a monthly patch window; critical CVEs are triaged and pushed immediately — we've automated build pipelines that rebuild images with patched packages and deploy with canary first. we also have automated vulnerability alerts in Slack and a weekly vuln mgmt meeting.

[06:18] Daniel Ortiz: monthly patch cadence is ok, but we need proof of quick-turn for criticals — like 48 hours SLA. do you have data on past critical patch SLAs?

[06:30] Priya Nair: we can pull historical patch timelines and include them in the remediation tracker. for Redwood Dedicated customers we can contract faster SLAs for criticals.

[06:45] Maya Patel: good. KMS/encryption — the pen test flagged a mis-keyed bucket config in staging that allowed weaker server-side encryption. is customer data at rest encrypted with customer-managed keys?

[06:58] Alex Chen: for hosted default we use service-managed KMS keys with envelope encryption; Dedicated and Private support customer-managed keys (CMKs) and HSM integrations. we log KMS usage and key rotation events. will send KMS whitepaper and attestation on rotation cadence.

[07:25] Samantha Lee: rotation cadence — is it automatic? how often?

[07:29] Priya Nair: default is annual rotation but you can request quarterly. for CMK integrations the customer controls rotation.

[07:40] Maya Patel: residency — we need all PHI to reside only in our chosen region (US-East). can you guarantee no cross-region backups or logs?

[07:52] Alex Chen: yes, for Private we can pin all storage and backups to your VPC region. For Dedicated we have region isolation controls and can enforce residency policies — we'll add residency proof and data flow diagrams.

[08:12] Daniel Ortiz: about audit evidence — we want to see the pen test findings, remediation evidence, vuln scans, and SOC2 report. timeline for those?

[08:22] Alex Chen: pen test annotated report we'll send by EOD Wednesday, remediation tracker within two business days after that (so by 2025-11-03 per today's call). SOC2/ISO cert links and prior audit pack we'll send by 2025-10-29.

[08:45] Priya Nair: i'll include the change PRs and build artifacts for the fixes we pushed, plus the CI run IDs and test logs.

[09:00] Maya Patel: great. on the medium items — TLS config on metrics — did the tester show client downgrade or was it theoretical?

[09:10] Priya Nair: they were able to negotiate weak ciphers against an older client emulator; we've removed legacy ciphers and forced TLS1.2+ on metrics endpoints. we'll show the handshake logs.

[09:28] Daniel Ortiz: any impact to observability stack? removing old ciphers might break older collectors. we have a few on-prem collectors still on older OS.

[09:39] Alex Chen: we'll provide a compatibility matrix and suggest a migration plan. collectors that can't be upgraded can proxy through an agent that handles TLS translation inside the network.

[09:55] Samantha Lee: what about RBAC and SSO — we need enterprise SAML + SCIM provisioning and role scoping.

[10:05] Priya Nair: Redwood supports SAML SSO, SCIM for provisioning, and fine-grained RBAC at the route/model level. we can map SCIM groups to roles and restrict model access per team. we'll share the RBAC matrix doc.

[10:22] Maya Patel: do you support session timeout and MFA enforcement for admin roles?

[10:29] Alex Chen: yes — session timeouts are configurable and we support enforced MFA for admin users via your identity provider.

[10:38] Maya Patel: ok, good. I want to drill into vulnerability management — do you run internal monthly network vulnerability scans and quarterly external scans?

[10:49] Priya Nair: internally we run continuous scanning (Aqua/Trivy for images) and scheduled weekly internal scans for infra; externally we run quarterly external pen tests plus ad-hoc scans for rolling infra changes. we also run automated dependency/vuln scanning on PRs.

[11:10] Daniel Ortiz: is there a public-facing CVE tracker or internal ticketing integration? we want tickets in JIRA with severity mapping.

[11:20] Alex Chen: we integrate with customer trackers via webhooks — we can push vulnerability tickets to your JIRA project with severity and remediation links. we'll include an example webhook config.

[11:34] Samantha Lee: the pen test referenced some container escapes on a specific runtime version — are you using runtime hardening and seccomp profiles?

[11:44] Priya Nair: yes — seccomp, AppArmor profiles in our container images, and immutable images in production. we also have a runtime policy that denies exec into critical containers. we've patched the offending images and rebuilt the registry.

[12:05] Maya Patel: good. can you also confirm your incident response runbook and who is our point of contact for incident coordination?

[12:15] Alex Chen: for customers, the AE/SE pair are primary contacts; for incident coordination we have a 24/7 on-call SRE team reachable via the security channel and escalation to an assigned CSM/Customer Success lead. we'll provide our incident runbook redacted for any sensitive internal ops.

[12:36] Daniel Ortiz: what about duration of retention for evidence — SOC2 needs six months of specific audit artifacts.

[12:45] Priya Nair: we can retain evidentiary artifacts for 12 months by default and longer on request, we also support exportable zip artifacts for audits.

[12:58] Maya Patel: perfect. any dependencies on third-party vendor responsiblities? if we require higher SLAs for patching, is that a contractual thing?

[13:10] Alex Chen: yes, faster patching SLAs and increased evidence retention are part of Dedicated/Enterprise contract add-ons. we can scope that in the SOW.

[13:24] Samantha Lee: one more — do you provide reproducible build attestations or SBOMs?

[13:30] Priya Nair: SBOMs for images and attestations for our build artifacts — yes, we produce SBOMs and sign build artifacts, will include examples.

[13:44] Maya Patel: ok this is helpful. let's talk timeline recap — pen test annotated report by 2025-10-29 EOD? you said EOD Wednesday earlier — that's 2025-10-29, correct?

[13:55] Alex Chen: correct, 2025-10-29 EOD for the annotated PDF. remediation tracker by 2025-11-03. follow-up to review evidence week of 2025-11-10.

[14:10] Daniel Ortiz: do you provide evidence of test harnesses and CI runs? we need artifacts to prove patch is applied and tests pass.

[14:20] Priya Nair: yes, we'll include CI build IDs, PR numbers, and deployment job logs.

[14:33] Maya Patel: excellent. any open concerns from Redwood's side about rolling fixes to our dedicated environment? downtime windows?

[14:43] Alex Chen: we'll coordinate maintenance windows with your team. most fixes are non-disruptive and rolled via canary; we'll schedule any restarts.

[14:56] Samantha Lee: regarding backup encryption, can you show proof that EBS snapshots / object storage are encrypted with CMKs?

[15:04] Priya Nair: we'll provide a sample snapshot manifest and KMS usage logs showing CMK IDs and keyrotation entries.

[15:18] Daniel Ortiz: great. are you able to provide a timeline of all remediation tasks, ownership and sign-off? that's necessary for our risk register.

[15:29] Alex Chen: yes — remediation tracker will include severity, owner (redwood vs customer), ETA, evidence link, and closure criteria. we'll format it as a shared spreadsheet and a JIRA backlog if you'd prefer.

[15:45] Maya Patel: JIRA backlog is preferred. please push tickets for Redwood-owed items so we can track.

[15:52] Priya Nair: understood — we'll open JIRA tickets with labels and link them in the tracker.

[16:05] Alex Chen: any other questions on SOC2/ISO — you asked earlier about attestation scope?

[16:12] Maya Patel: yes scope: do you include third-party vendors like cloud providers in your SOC2 or is it limited to Redwood's control plane?

[16:22] Alex Chen: SOC2 covers Redwood's control plane and services; cloud provider controls are considered complementary. we'll provide the SOC2 report and the complementary responsibility matrix.

[16:38] Samantha Lee: ok. one last thing — can we run an independence verification pen test with our third-party vendor and share results back?

[16:48] Priya Nair: absolutely. we can coordinate scoping. if they need ephemeral test accounts or timeboxed access, we can provision those.

[17:00] Maya Patel: perfect. i think that's all for the review. recap and next steps please.

[17:08] Alex Chen: quick recap: deliver annotated pen test report by 2025-10-29, remediation tracker by 2025-11-03, SOC2/ISO docs by 2025-10-29, KMS whitepaper and RBAC matrix by 2025-10-29. we'll open JIRA tickets for Redwood-ownership items and share evidence (CI IDs, PRs, logs).

[17:30] Priya Nair: action items: i'll share the annotated report and remediation tracker, Alex will send SOC2 links + KMS whitepaper, and we'll provision any test accounts you need.

[17:45] Maya Patel: thanks. please include a note on the audit log retention and prove forwarder config.

[17:55] Alex Chen: will do. thanks everyone, we'll follow up via email and set the follow-up calendar invite for the week of 2025-11-10.

[18:05] (end transcript)

Notes: transcript includes minor transcription errors and informal speech. References: shared file: /links/pen-test-annotated-sequoia-2025-10-27.pdf (shared in chat), RBAC matrix: /links/rbac-matrix-sequoia.pdf, KMS whitepaper: /links/redwood-kms-whitepaper.pdf

Summary section (auto-gen, optional): Pen test surfaced 3 high-risk items (exposed staging admin ingress, RBAC bypass in integration component, weak TLS ciphers on metrics endpoint). Redwood patched issues and will provide remediation evidence and CI artifacts. Customer requested residency proof, audit logs, SOC2/ISO attestation, and JIRA tickets for tracking.

- Priya Nair: share annotated pen test PDF + remediation tracker - due 2025-11-03
- Maya Patel: provide data residency constraints - due 2025-11-10
